To view service quotas for Amazon Bedrock, do one of the following:\\n\\n* Follow the steps at Viewing service\\n quotas and select **Amazon Bedrock** as the service.\\n* Refer to Amazon Bedrock service\\n quotas in the AWS General Reference.\\n\\nThe following quotas apply specifically to managed knowledge bases:\\n\\nManaged knowledge base quotas\\n\\n| Quota | Default value | Adjustable |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Maximum managed knowledge bases per account, per Region | 10,000 | No |\\n| Maximum data sources per knowledge base | 200 | Yes |\\n| Maximum concurrent ingestion jobs per knowledge base | 50 | No |\\n| Maximum raw data storage per knowledge base | 10 TB | Yes |\\n| Maximum query input characters per `Retrieve` or `AgenticRetrieveStream` request (English text) | 10,000 | No |\\n| Maximum `Retrieve` requests per minute (RPM), per knowledge base | 600 (supports burst of 25 requests per second (RPS)) | Yes |\\n| Maximum `AgenticRetrieveStream` requests per minute, per account | 300 | Yes |\\n| Maximum retrieval instructions per account, per Region | 50 | Yes |\\n| Maximum versions per retrieval instruction | 50 | Yes |\\n| Maximum total characters across the fields of a retrieval instruction | 24,000 | Yes |\\n\\nTo request adjustable quota increases, follow the steps at Requesting a\\nquota increase, or contact your AWS account team\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-quotas.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Sync your data with your Amazon Bedrock knowledge base\",\"context\":\"#### Using API\\n\\nTo ingest your data into your knowledge base and sync with your latest data, send a StartIngestionJob request with a Agents for Amazon Bedrock build-time endpoint. Specify the `knowledgeBaseId` and `dataSourceId`.\\nYou can also stop a data ingestion job that is currently running by sending a StopIngestionJob request. Specify the `dataSourceId`, `ingestionJobId`, and `knowledgeBaseId`. A data ingestion job must be currently running in order\\nto stop data ingestion. You can send a `StartIngestionJob` request again to ingest the rest of your data when you are ready.\\n\\nUse the `ingestionJobId` returned in the response in a GetIngestionJob request with a Agents for Amazon Bedrock build-time endpoint to track the status of the ingestion job.
